-class BasicTokenizer(Tokenizer):
+from operator import countOf
+
+from .base import Tokenizer, get_stats, merge, apply_merges, _count_elements
+
+
+def merge_update(ids, pair, idx, stats):
+    """
+    Same result as merge(ids, pair, idx), but also updates stats (pair counts
+    of ids) in place so that it equals get_stats() of the returned list.
+    Only the pairs around replaced runs change, so only those are recounted.
+    """
+    p0, p1 = pair
+    k = ids.count(p0)
+    newids = []
+    extend = newids.extend
+    append = newids.append
+    index = ids.index
+    last = len(ids) - 1
+    same = p0 == p1
+    regions = [] # (s, e): old positions [s, e) replaced by consecutive idx
+    s = e = -1
+    i = 0
+    while k:
+        j = index(p0, i)
+        k -= 1
+        if j < last and ids[j+1] == p1:
+            if same:
+                k -= 1 # ids[j+1] was an occurrence of p0 too
+            if j != e:
+                # not adjacent to the previous replacement: start a new run
+                if e >= 0:
+                    regions.append((s, e))
+                s = j
+                extend(ids[i:j])
+            append(idx)
+            e = i = j + 2
+        else:
+            extend(ids[i:j+1])
+            i = j + 1
+    if e >= 0:
+        regions.append((s, e))
+    extend(ids[i:])
+    # update the pair counts: drop the old pairs touching each run, add the new
+    stats_get = stats.get
+    touched = []
+    for s, e in regions:
+        lo = s - 1 if s else 0
+        old_w = ids[lo:e+1]
+        for p in zip(old_w, old_w[1:]):
+            stats[p] -= 1
+            touched.append(p)
+        new_w = ids[lo:s]
+        new_w += [idx] * ((e - s) >> 1)
+        new_w += ids[e:e+1]
+        _count_elements(stats, zip(new_w, new_w[1:]))
+    for p in touched:
+        if stats_get(p) == 0:
+            del stats[p]
+    return newids
+
+
+class BasicTokenizer(Tokenizer):

+        vocab = {idx: bytes([idx]) for idx in range(256)} # int -> bytes
+        # count up the number of times every consecutive pair appears (once);
+        # merge_update keeps the counts in sync with ids afterwards
+        stats = get_stats(ids)
+        stats_get = stats.get
+        for i in range(num_merges):
+            # find the pair with the highest count; ties go to the pair that
+            # occurs first in ids, which is what max() over a freshly counted
+            # get_stats(ids) (insertion order = first occurrence) would pick
+            pair = max(stats, key=stats_get)
+            top = stats[pair]
+            if countOf(stats.values(), top) > 1:
+                cands = {p for p, c in stats.items() if c == top}
+                pair = next(filter(cands.__contains__, zip(ids, ids[1:])))
+            # mint a new token: assign it the next available id
+            idx = 256 + i
+            # replace all occurrences of pair in ids with idx
+            ids = merge_update(ids, pair, idx, stats)
+            # save the merge
+            merges[pair] = idx
+            vocab[idx] = vocab[pair[0]] + vocab[pair[1]]
+            # prints
+            if verbose:
+                print(f"merge {i+1}/{num_merges}: {pair} -> {idx} ({vocab[idx]}) had {top} occurrences")
